title: A fraction of an amount
summary: Share apples equally and take some of the parts. Then scale a recipe up and down.
guide: This studio covers Year 2–3 work on fractions of amounts. To find {{frac:1/3}} of 12, share 12 into 3 equal parts and take one part. To find {{frac:3/4}} of 20, make 4 equal parts of 20 and take 3 of them.

The {{term:denominator}} says how many equal parts to share into; the {{term:numerator}} says how many parts to take. A common slip is to give the numerator or denominator itself as the answer (saying {{frac:1/3}} of 12 is 3).
The last two missions make a recipe 3 times bigger and then {{frac:1/3}} of the size: every amount changes in the same way.

engine.instruction-tap: Tap a + button or an empty space.
engine.instruction-split: Tap a counter to colour the columns.
engine.instruction-cross: Tap a counter to cross it out.

third-of-twelve.title: {{frac:1/3}} of 12
third-of-twelve.prompt: Fatemeh has 12 apples. She gives {{frac:1/3}} of them to Ali. Share the apples equally between 3 plates. What is {{frac:1/3}} of 12?
third-of-twelve.hint: {{frac:1/3}} means one of 3 equal parts. Tap the + buttons in turn until the basket is empty. Then count the apples on one plate.
third-of-twelve.success: Well done! One plate has 4 apples. 12 ÷ 3 = 4, so {{frac:1/3}} of 12 is 4.
third-of-twelve.why: What is {{frac:2/3}} of 12? How do you know?
third-of-twelve.model: 8. {{frac:1/3}} of 12 is one plate, which is 4 apples. {{frac:2/3}} is two plates: 4 + 4 = 8.

feedback.too-many: There are still apples in the basket. Finish sharing.
feedback.not-equal: The plates are not equal. A third only makes sense when the parts are equal.
feedback.denominator: 3 is the number of parts (the denominator). Count the apples in one part.
feedback.subtracted: You worked out 12 − 3. We shared 12 into 3 equal parts; count one part.
feedback.two-parts: That's two plates, which is {{frac:2/3}}. Count just one plate.
feedback.too-big: Count the apples on one plate again.
feedback.too-small: Count the apples on one plate again.
feedback.empty: Now tap the number for your answer.

three-quarters.title: {{frac:3/4}} of 20
three-quarters.prompt: These 20 counters are in 4 equal columns. Each column is {{frac:1/4}} of the counters. Keep 3 columns red and make the rest yellow. What is {{frac:3/4}} of 20?
three-quarters.hint: Tap a counter in the 3rd column. Each column has 5 counters, so 3 columns: 5, 10, …
three-quarters.success: Well done! Each column is 5 counters and 3 columns are 15. {{frac:3/4}} of 20 is 15.
three-quarters.why: Why did you divide 20 by 4 first and then multiply by 3?
three-quarters.model: The denominator 4 says make 4 equal parts of 20: 20 ÷ 4 = 5. The numerator 3 says take 3 parts: 3 × 5 = 15.

feedback.wrong-colors: You need 3 red columns and 1 yellow column. Tap a counter in the 3rd column.
feedback.one-part: 5 is only one column, which is {{frac:1/4}}. We want 3 columns.
feedback.numerator: 3 is the number of columns (the numerator). Count the counters in those 3 columns.
feedback.denominator: 4 is the number of parts (the denominator). Count the red counters.
feedback.empty: Now tap the number for your answer.

three-cakes.title: Three times as much
three-cakes.prompt: Sara needs 4 eggs for 1 cake. She wants to bake 3 cakes. Put eggs in for cake 2 and cake 3 too. How many eggs does she need altogether?
three-cakes.hint: Tap the empty spaces so that each cake has 4 eggs.
three-cakes.success: Well done! 3 cakes with 4 eggs each: 3 × 4 = 12
three-cakes.why: If Sara makes only half a cake, how many eggs does she need? Why?
three-cakes.model: 2 eggs. {{frac:1/2}} of 4 means 4 shared into 2 equal parts: 4 ÷ 2 = 2.

feedback.too-few: Each cake needs 4 eggs. Fill the empty spaces.
feedback.too-many: That's too many. Tap an egg to take it away.
feedback.added: You worked out 3 + 4. But there are 3 cakes and each needs 4 eggs.
feedback.two-cakes: That's the eggs for 2 cakes. There are three cakes.
feedback.empty: Now tap the number for your answer.

soup-for-two.title: Soup for 2
soup-for-two.prompt: Hassan makes soup for 6 people with 12 potatoes. Each row is for 2 people. Today there are only 2 people, which is {{frac:1/3}} of them. Cross out the potatoes he doesn't need. How many potatoes does he need?
soup-for-two.hint: 6 people is 3 rows. Keep just one row; cross out the other 2 rows.
soup-for-two.success: Well done! {{frac:1/3}} of 12 is 4. 12 ÷ 3 = 4 potatoes for 2 people.
soup-for-two.why: If 4 people come ({{frac:2/3}} of them), how many potatoes are needed? Why?
soup-for-two.model: 8. Every 2 people need one row of 4. 4 people is 2 rows: 4 + 4 = 8. So {{frac:2/3}} of 12 is 8.

feedback.too-many: There are still extra potatoes. Keep only one row.
feedback.too-few: You crossed out too many. 2 people need one whole row. Tap a potato to remove its cross.
feedback.counted-crossed: You crossed out 8. Count the potatoes without a cross.
feedback.denominator: 3 is the number of rows. Count the potatoes in one row.
feedback.halved: 6 is half of 12. But 2 people is {{frac:1/3}} of 6 people, not half.
feedback.people: 2 is the number of people. Count the potatoes.
feedback.too-big: Count the potatoes without a cross again.
feedback.too-small: Count the potatoes without a cross again.
feedback.empty: Now tap the number for your answer.
